To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of gallium to Pd/SiBunit results in a decrease in the activity and selectivity of the catalyst in the liquid-phase acetylenic hydrogenation.
the Pd-Ga catalysts are more active and selective for ethylene production in the acetylene hydrogenations, compared to the Pd/Sibun catalysts.
the structural characteristics and catalytical properties of Pd-Gal/Sibunit catalyst are determined by the surface gallium oxide film that forms on the bimetallic particle surface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the structural characteristics of Pd/SiO 2 and Pd–Ga/SiO  2 catalysts for the hydrogenation of acetaldehyde.
the synthesis of a novel class of Pd-based catalysts with high activity and selectivity for liquid-phase acethylene hydrogenation.

the synthesis of Pd/SiB and Pd-Gal/SiB catalysts for the selective hydrogenation of acetaldehyde to ethylene in the liquid phase, the structural and catalytic properties, and the effect of gallium additives on the catalytic properties of these catalysts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the addition of gallium oxide to the Pd/Sibunits catalyst does not lead to any significant improvement in its activity and selectivity in liquid-phase acetylenic hydrogenation, which is in contrast to its effect on the gas-phase hydrogenation of propylene.
the addition of Ga to the Pd/Sib unit system leads to a decrease in the activity and selectivity of the catalysts for the hydrogenation of acetyl-ene to ethylene.

the presence of a surface film of gallia covering the surface of Pd-Gal/Sibunit particles is responsible for the lower activity of this catalyst, as well as for its lower selectivity to ethene, in comparison with Pd/Sibunite.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Pd/Sibunite and Pd-Gal/Sibunite catalysts were synthesized and characterized by EXAFS and HRTEM.
the Pd-Ga bimetallic catalysts are more selective than the monometallic Pd catalyst for the hydrogenation of acetic acid to ethanol, but the Pd catalyst is more active for this reaction.

the Pd-Ga catalysts are more active and selective than the Pd catalysts for the hydrogenation of acetic acid, and the selectivity to acetic acid is higher in the case of the Pd-Gal catalyst than the Pd-Gall catalyst.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Pd/Sibunits catalysts have a higher activity and selectivity than the Pd-Ga/sibunits ones.
, in order to achieve a high activity of the bimetallic catalyst, the active centers of palladium and gallium oxide should be located at a distance from each other.
the use of Sibunit as a catalyst support is promising in the development of new catalysts for the hydrogenation of acyclic olefins.
